cases.title: GitLab.com 2017 primary database data removal

source_documents.summary: Primary narrative source for the 2017 database outage, data loss, failed backups, and linked follow-up work.
Follow-up issue to differentiate production and staging shells so operators can identify host and environment.
Follow-up issue to move backup monitoring to Prometheus/Slack and graph backup status.
Follow-up issue to investigate point-in-time recovery and continuous archiving.
Follow-up issue to increase production database snapshots from daily to hourly.
Follow-up issue to test PostgreSQL backup restores automatically against real tables.
Pre-existing public issue for staging migration execution and rollback testing.
Public product issue identifying hard deletion as a policy gap after user/project removal.

source_assertions.phrase: accidental removal of data from our primary database server
source_assertions.summary: The postmortem identifies accidental removal from the primary database as the outage cause.

source_assertions.phrase: lost modifications to database data such as projects, comments, user accounts, issues and snippets
source_assertions.summary: The postmortem identifies concrete production-data classes that were lost.

source_assertions.phrase: both finding and using backups failed completely
source_assertions.summary: The postmortem identifies backup/recovery failure as part of the incident.

source_assertions.phrase: Use bold red for production, normal yellow for staging
source_assertions.summary: A public follow-up issue identifies environment confusion between production and staging as repair-relevant operational state.

source_assertions.phrase: Backup alerts should instead use Prometheus alerts and be sent to Slack.
source_assertions.summary: A public follow-up issue requires executable monitoring over backups.
A public follow-up issue identifies PITR/continuous archiving as a needed recovery mechanism.

source_assertions.phrase: This has proven to be inadequate as a recovery technique.
source_assertions.summary: A public follow-up issue says daily LVM snapshots were insufficient and should become hourly.

source_assertions.phrase: Automated testing of recovering PostgreSQL database backups
source_assertions.summary: A public follow-up issue requires recurring executable backup-restore tests.

source_assertions.phrase: Tool for executing and reverting Rails migrations on staging
source_assertions.summary: A public issue proposes executable staging migration tests with automatic rollback.

source_assertions.phrase: Removal of users by spam should not hard delete
source_assertions.summary: A public product issue identifies hard deletion as unsafe operational behavior.

cases.avoidance_claim: Patchline would not certify the reconstructed destructive primary-data operation because public sources establish primary-data loss, backup/recovery gaps, and follow-up remediation work that map directly to protected-table, snapshot, rollback, and source-grounded recovery obligations.

cases.title: GitHub 2018 MySQL split-brain write divergence

source_assertions.phrase: displaying of information that was out of date and inconsistent
source_assertions.summary: The post-incident analysis identifies stale and inconsistent user-visible state.

source_assertions.phrase: both data centers now contained writes that were not present in the other data center
source_assertions.summary: The analysis identifies divergent writes across database sites.

source_assertions.phrase: manual reconciliation for a few seconds of database writes is still in progress
source_assertions.summary: The analysis identifies reconciliation work for writes after the incident.

cases.avoidance_claim: Patchline would flag the divergent logical-record writes before declaring recovery complete, forcing a convergence/reconciliation proof instead of accepting inconsistent derived state.
